sqlite_read_only.limitation: Read transactions succeeding do not prove the writer queue is uncongested. No write-lock probe was executed.

stack_sampling.limitation: Nonblocking samples can be approximate and do not establish exclusive time spent in a frame.

source_findings.finding: The heartbeat coroutine calls lock.heartbeat synchronously after each5s asyncio sleep. The heartbeat reads its diagnostic payload and calls os.utime on the event-loop thread.
GET connections/me invokes current_agent_revisions without persist=False. The default persist=True uses a write unit-of-work/BEGIN IMMEDIATE even though this is an observation route.
Inventory publication runs in asyncio.to_thread; discovery separately hashes native binaries in worker threads. It shares host CPU/I/O and the canonical SQLite writer queue.

conclusion: Synchronous filesystem heartbeat on the event loop and writer participation of GET connections/me are concrete product risks. Host CPU saturation is independently observed. Current evidence does not prove a permanent SQLite deadlock or isolate one exclusive root cause. Preserve both adoption failures and investigate these paths without retrying the campaign or increasing timeouts.
